title: Replication Protocol & Partial Resync (PSYNC)
summary: Understand master-replica replication, replication IDs, byte offsets, and how the circular backlog buffer enables PSYNC partial recovery after transient disconnects.

steps.title: Inspect replication role and master offset
steps.explanation: Query INFO replication to view role, master_repl_offset, and connected_slaves count. The master replication offset increments with every written byte.

steps.title: Write a payload and track offset progression
steps.explanation: Send a write command. Notice how the primary appends the exact RESP serialized command into its 1MB replication backlog ring buffer and updates master_repl_offset.

steps.title: Evaluate PSYNC Partial vs Full Resynchronization
steps.explanation: When a replica disconnects and reconnects, it sends `PSYNC <replid> <offset>`. If the replica's offset is still within the primary's circular backlog, the master responds `+CONTINUE` (instant partial sync). If too much time has passed, it falls back to transferring a full RDB snapshot.
steps.hint: Run: ROLE to inspect current node topology.
